newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale says U.S. grain remarks unhelpful.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale says U.S. grain remarks unhelpful.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale upbraided the United States for remarks on Thursday suggesting Canada's willingness to limit its grain exports.
"It's entirely unhelpful in the context of our bilateral relationships, and the United States should make an effort to be a little more accurate," he told reporters.
Reacting to Congressional testimony by a U.S. agriculture official, Goodale repeated his denial that Canadian grain exports were running unusually high and that Canada was willing to limit them.
"The U.S. allegations are completely, utterly, absolutely unfounded and wrong," he said, adding the words he said were from his departmental officials: "No bloody way."

U.S. Department of Agriculture officials are due in Ottawa on April 25 for previously scheduled consultations on a number of trade issues, and Goodale said this issue was one Canada would be planning to put to rest.

"We have suggested to the United States for quite some time that it might well be helpful, rather than dealing with these political flashpoints, that we establish some regular, ongoing method of dialogue so that there can be an exchange of factual information.

"We're still more than interested in pursuing that at a government-to-government level, at a grain industry-to-grain industry level in the private sector. We're also interested in any other technique that can get all this other fallacious garbage off the table and let's talk about the real facts."
